figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Current progress in Taxol oxetane ring formation. (A) Abbreviated Taxol biosynthetic pathway. CYP725A4, taxadiene-5α-hydroxylase.
5αAT, 5α-O-acetyltransferase. (B) Previously proposed mechanisms for Taxol oxetane ring formation. (C) Structures of two naturally occurring
advanced taxanes containing an unacetylated oxetane ring moiety. (D) Acetylation of the oxetane ring of 4-deacyl baccatin III shown in a previous
study. 10βAT, 10β-O-acetyltransferase. (E) Our hypothesis of the Taxol oxetane ring biosynthesis.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Metabolic engineering for improving taxadiene production in yeast. (A) Comparison of taxadiene production by yeast strains AM144-1,
AM151-1, AM153-1, and AM158-1, in which TXS is localized in the cytosol. Detailed genotyping for each strain is given in Table S4. Error bars
show the standard deviation of the mean of three independent replicates. (B) Comparison of taxadiene production by cytosolic or peroxisomal
localization of TXS in strains AM158-1 and AM158-2. (C) GC−MS extracted ion chromatogram (EIC; m/z = 122) of AM158 cells
compartmentalizing TXS in the cytosol (black) or the peroxisome (orange).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. UPLC-HRMS extracted ion chromatogram (EIC; positive
mode, m/z = 305.2475 ± 0.01) of the yeast EtOAc extracts generated
from coexpressing TXS with CYP725A4, CYP725A2, and
CYP725A54. A yeast strain only expressing TXS was used as a
control.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. Biosynthesis of dioxygenated taxanes in tobacco. (A)
UPLC-HRMS extracted ion chromatogram (EIC; positive mode, m/z
= 305.2475 ± 0.01) of the tobacco MeOH extracts generated from
coexpressing TXS with CYP725A4, CYP725A2, and CYP725A54.
The P19 gene was coexpressed in all samples to help suppress gene
silencing. (B) Structures of dioxygenated taxanes 1−5 elucidated by
NMR analysis.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 5. Biosynthesis of taxologenic oxetane from both endotaxadiene and exotaxadiene. (A) Production and isolation of endotaxadiene (6) and
exotaxadiene (7) in tobacco leaves indicated by GC−MS analysis (total ion chromatogram). Endotaxadiene (6) and exotaxadiene (7) were
identified by the comparison of their GC−MS spectra.29 (B) Production of taxologenic oxetane (3) in CYP725A4 expressing tobacco leaves after
feeding endotaxadiene (6) and exotaxadiene (7) indicated by UPLC-HRMS analysis (EIC; positive mode, m/z = 305.2475 ± 0.01). (C) Dead-end
product, OCT (9), was detected in CYP725A4-expressing tobacco leaves after feeding endotaxadiene (6) but not exotaxadiene (7). OCT standard
(9) was purified from tobacco leaves coexpressing TXS and CYP725A4 and identified by NMR (data shown in Table S10). (D) Proposed
biosynthetic routine of the taxologenic oxetane (3).
